title: Issue/PR workflows must share a per-issue concurrency group key, not github.run_id
answers: repeated edits to an issue trigger parallel workflow runs
why does my issue bot workflow run twice at once on the same issue
concurrency group for issue-triggered GitHub workflow
labeling workflow runs in parallel for the same pull request
body:
Invariant: concurrency.group in issue- or PR-triggered workflows under .github/workflows must key on the issue or PR, as `${{ github.workflow }}-${{ github.event.issue.number }}` (issue-only triggers) or `${{ github.workflow }}-${{ github.event.issue.number || github.event.pull_request.number }}` (dual issues/pull_request_target triggers).
Symptom: repeated opened/edited events on one issue or PR start overlapping bot runs.
Root cause: the group was `${{ github.run_id }}`, which is unique per run, so no two runs ever share a group and nothing serializes them.
What breaks if skipped: a single-number key is empty for the other event type on dual-trigger workflows, so the `||` fallback is required in labeling.yml.
Constraints: cancel-in-progress stays false in these files; the PR relies on job-level `if:` conditions to gate the work, so cancelling in-flight runs is not used. Enforced only by the YAML concurrency block, not by any test.
applies: Applies to GitHub workflows triggered by issues or pull requests whose concurrency group must serialize repeated events per item; not to push, schedule or workflow_dispatch workflows, which have no issue number.
says: Editing an issue repeatedly triggers overlapping bot runs at the same time.
Automated labeling bot runs multiple instances concurrently when a pull request is updated.
Issue automation bot posts duplicate comments when an issue is edited in rapid succession.
Ensure automated workflows for an issue run sequentially rather than in parallel.
Repeated changes to a pull request cause simultaneous automated triage actions.
search: GitHub workflows triggered by issues or pull requests must serialize per item by keying concurrency.group on the workflow and issue or pull request number rather than github.run_id. Dual-trigger workflows require a fallback expression to prevent empty keys across both event types, as in .github/workflows/labeling.yml. Workflows keep cancel-in-progress set to false, relying on job-level if conditions rather than run cancellation. The rule applies to .github/workflows/close-security-issues.yml, issue-warning.yml, and labeling.yml, and does not apply to push, schedule, or workflow_dispatch triggers.
